Expected results are small enough to verify by hand.

terms.meaning: Finding the most relevant documents for a question, so the AI can read them.
The time after which nothing may be shown to the AI.
Permission to use content from a particular source.
Always giving the same result for the same input.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports search tools and sets cutoff
sections.what: Brings in the test tools, the model input builder, the search functions, and sets a fixed snapshot cutoff time.
sections.why: Likely reason: the tests use the same functions the app uses, so they check the real search.
sections.watch_out: The cutoff is fixed, so documents dated after it are always excluded in these tests.

sections.name: docs, canUse
sections.title: Four sample documents
sections.what: Defines four small documents with dates and sources, one from an unlicensed blog that must be excluded.
sections.why: Likely reason: a small, varied set makes the expected results easy to check.
sections.watch_out: Tests rely on these exact documents, so adding or changing one may change the top result.

sections.name: retrieval with a temporal filter (retrieval)
sections.title: Checks search and cutoff rules
sections.what: Checks no document after the cutoff is returned, unlicensed sources and non-matching or empty queries return nothing, and the result count is capped. Checks ties go to the most recent document, then to id. Checks the model input drops facts and text after the cutoff, and that the domain search applies both the source and time rules.
sections.why: Likely reason: these rules stop the AI from reading the future or unlicensed content.
sections.watch_out: The time cutoff is the main safety rule. If it fails, the AI could see information from after the snapshot.

summary: Tests the search step that finds documents for the AI to read, making sure nothing after the snapshot time or from an unlicensed source gets through.
purpose: Protects the time and rights rules for what the AI can read, so the answer only uses what was known and allowed at the snapshot.
why: Likely reason: the AI must not see future facts or unlicensed content, which would break accuracy and the terms of use. Reason not stated in the code for the tie-break rule.
how: Creates four small documents with dates and sources. Checks the search never returns a document after the cutoff, drops unlicensed sources, empty and non-matching queries, and caps the number of results. Checks that ties go to the most recent, then to id. Checks the model input drops facts and text after the cutoff, and that the domain search applies both rules.
inputs: Four sample documents, a search query, a cutoff time and a source check.
outputs: A ranked list of matching documents, and a model input containing only allowed facts and text.
risks: Tests depend on the exact documents and dates. Adding documents may change which result is top.
debug: If a test fails, check the cutoff time and the source check first, then the matching rule for the search terms.
